bib.title: Mutual Reasoning Makes Smaller LLMs Stronger Problem-Solvers

question: Can small language models improve their reasoning at inference time, without fine-tuning or a superior teacher model?
hypothesis: Agreement between two similar-capability SLMs (one generating via MCTS, one completing partial trajectories) signals a correct trajectory, and a richer action space gives better candidates than single-action self-exploration.
contributions: rStar: self-play mutual generation-discrimination reasoning for SLMs without fine-tuning
MCTS with a 5-action human-like reasoning action space
Mutual reasoning consistency: a second SLM completes masked trajectories and agreement marks them valid
Evaluation on five SLMs and five reasoning tasks

method.summary: A target SLM builds a search tree with MCTS using five reasoning actions (32 rollouts). A second SLM (Phi3-mini-4k) is given a random-length prefix of each candidate trajectory and completes it; trajectories whose answer matches are kept, and the target SLM picks the one with highest reward times terminal confidence.
method.task: math and commonsense reasoning with small LMs at inference time

datasets.name: MATH-500
datasets.source: Hendrycks et al., 2021; subset following Wang et al. 2024b and Lightman et al. 2023

inference.decoding: MCTS with UCT selection, 32 rollouts, then trajectory selection
inference.samples: 32 MCTS rollouts per question; baselines SC sampled 8, 64, 128 times; single run, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: few-shot CoT prompts per action (A1 and A2/A4 use 4 and 8 exemplars of GSM8K style; A3 least-to-most with 4 exemplars; A5 rephrase with 8 exemplars), Appendix A.3

parameters.actions: A1 one-step thought, A2 remaining steps, A3 next sub-question with answer, A4 re-answer sub-question, A5 rephrase question
parameters.max_depth_d: 8 for MATH, 5 for all other tasks
parameters.max_nodes_per_depth: 5 for A1 and A3, 1 for the other actions
parameters.discriminator_split: prefix cut randomly between 20% and 80% of steps
parameters.final_score: reward multiplied by terminal node confidence

other.cost: 166.81 avg calls and 367.1k generated tokens per GSM8K question on LLaMA2-7B; 32 rollouts over GSM8K test set about 4.5 days on one A100 per model

eval.protocol: single reported number per cell, no seeds or significance tests stated; Table 1 ablation uses 200 sampled GSM8K questions

availability.code: stated as 'will be available' with a link placeholder

prompts.text: You are an AI assistant to help me rephrase questions by splitting the question context into conditions. In your rephrased question, remember to fully express the information in the original question.
Given a question, please decompose it into sub-questions. For each sub-question, please answer it in a complete sentence, ending with "The answer is <a numeric answer>".

limits: Cost is high: about 150-170 model calls and 350k tokens per GSM8K question, 4.5 days per model on one A100 for the test set.
Code not released at time of writing; temperature, UCT constant c, sampling parameters and seeds are not stated.
Single runs without variance; the 200-question sample in Table 1 is small.
MATH evaluated only on 500 problems and only two models because of LaTeX instruction-following.
Discriminator is Phi3-mini; gains with GPT-4 are small, so authors do not test far stronger or weaker mismatches beyond the Table 5 list.
